title: Impact Player Chess: Which Substitution Gives Chennai Super Kings the Biggest Edge?
dek: The impact-player rule turned team selection into a match-day decision. Which substitution gives Chennai Super Kings the biggest edge? The before-and-after numbers frame the question.
excerpt: Chennai Super Kings' totals have risen no faster than the league's since the impact-player rule arrived in 2023. The substitution record itself is not in public data, so the choice has to be reasoned from its effects.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: A Twelfth Player, Chosen Late
body: Since 2023 each side can bring in a substitute who bats or bowls in full. The obvious use is to bat deep in the first innings and swap in a bowler for the second, or the reverse when chasing.
The effect on scoring is visible. Chennai Super Kings averaged {{ev:ip-rb}} runs per innings in 2019–2022 and {{ev:ip-ri}} since 2023; the rest of the league went from {{ev:ip-lb}} to {{ev:ip-li}}.

sections.heading: What Changed in the Field
body: CSK used {{ev:ip-bb}} bowlers per innings before the rule and {{ev:ip-bi}} after it. A deeper bench of bowling options can change how overs are shared, even if the core five still bowl most of them.
The comparison table sets each measure for CSK beside the rest of the league.

sections.heading: Choosing the Substitution
body: The highest-value substitution is the one that fills the side's weakest phase. If the death bowling is the weak link, an extra specialist for the second innings is worth more than an extra batter; if the middle order collapses, the reverse.
For CSK, the phase-by-phase comparisons elsewhere in this series identify which phase that is.

sections.heading: What the Data Cannot See
body: Public ball-by-ball data does not record which player was the impact substitute, so the effect of each choice cannot be measured directly. The before-and-after comparison also mixes the rule with a general rise in scoring.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Substitute for the Weakest Phase
body: The rule has not especially lifted Chennai Super Kings' scoring relative to the league. The edge comes from using the substitution to patch the side's weakest phase each match.
Recording every substitution and the phase it was meant to strengthen would let the franchise measure the choice directly.
